sections.h2: Who records deeds in Cass County, Michigan?
sections.html:
In Cass County the elected Clerk/Register handles land records along with circuit court files, marriage licenses, vital records and elections. The office is at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, in Cassopolis, with phone 269-445-4464 and fax 269-445-4406. Call ahead to confirm counter hours before you drive in with an original deed.

The county runs a basic deed search for occasional users. Searching the index by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number is free, but viewing, printing or saving an image costs $1 per page plus a processing fee. The Register's office will locate a single document on request, yet it has no authority to search real property records or compile a list of recorded instruments for you.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a document in Cass County?
sections.html:
Since October 1, 2016, every recording in Cass County has cost $30 no matter how many pages it has. A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3 for each instrument. The statewide basis is MCL 600.2567. Do not staple a check to the document.

  • Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of them need a county treasurer tax certification, and its $5 fee can go on the same check as the recording fee.
  • UCC terminations and fixture filings are $30 each; financing statements are filed with the State of Michigan only.
  • Copies: $1 per page, $5 for a plat of record, $5 by fax, and $5 to certify.
  • Searches: 50 cents per year with a $5 minimum, $3 per name for a state or federal tax lien certificate, and $6 for a financing statement certificate on one debtor name.

sections.h2: What does Cass County require on a deed?
sections.html:
The county posts a twenty-point checklist. Some points repeat the format rules in MCL 565.201, and a few go further than other Michigan counties spell out.

  • A complete legal description of the property.
  • The notary acknowledgment showing the notary's signature, county and state of certification, the names of the people acknowledging, and the notary's commission expiration date, plus the state and county where the paper was signed.
  • A notary seal for any out-of-state notary.
  • Only the last four digits of a Social Security number, unless a law or court order requires more.
  • An affidavit about the correction when an original document is re-recorded.
  • A certified death certificate recorded with the instrument, or referenced by liber and page, when a grantor is described as survivor of someone.
  • The consideration stated on the face of the deed. The phrase "other good and valuable consideration" is allowed only with an affidavit.

Margins, type and paper follow the statewide rule: 2 1/2 inches blank at the top of page one, 1/2 inch elsewhere, black ink of at least 10-point, white paper of at least 20-pound weight, and sheets between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches.

sections.h2: What does a Cass County tax certification actually cover?
sections.html:
Under MCL 211.135, the certificate comes in two layers. The county or state treasurer reports whether any tax liens or tax titles are held against the parcel and whether taxes have been paid for the five years before the instrument's date. The city, village or township treasurer where the land sits reports on tax titles and tax sale certificates, and whether those tax titles, certificates and special assessments were redeemed for the same five years.

Timing can matter. If the paper is presented on or after March 1, before the local treasurer has returned the current year's delinquent taxes, the county treasurer notes that the current delinquent return was not available. The register may not refuse to record on that basis alone.

A Cass County seller whose parcel has a tax certificate or special assessment sold against it should get a payoff figure from the village or township before the closing date, since the statute asks for proof of redemption.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Cass County sale carry?
sections.html:
Cass County follows the statewide rates: 55 cents per $500 for the county under MCL 207.504 and $3.75 per $500 for the state under MCL 207.525, with any part of a $500 block counted as a full block. At $218,000, the Census median owner-occupied value for Cass County, that is 436 blocks.

Cass County transfer tax at sample prices (statutory rates; $218,000 is the Census 2020-2024 median value)
Sale priceCounty taxState taxTotal due
$120,000$132.00$900.00$1,032.00
$218,000$239.80$1,635.00$1,874.80
$350,000$385.00$2,625.00$3,010.00

A sale that includes personal property is taxed only on the real estate when the deed or an affidavit states the two values separately.

sections.h2: Which Cass County transfers are exempt from transfer tax?
sections.html:
The exemption lists in MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526 overlap heavily. The ones that come up most often in a Cass County house sale or family transfer are these.

  • A land contract, until the buyer has paid the full price and legal title passes.
  • A quitclaim deed whose only purpose is to confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • A deed that straightens a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • A joint tenancy created among people when at least one already owned the land.
  • A conveyance from one spouse, or both, that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • Under the state act only: a gift deed to a child, stepchild, grandchild or their adopted equivalents, and a conveyance between an entity and its owners when the entity dissolves.

A deed that claims one of these must still be recorded in proper form, so ask the Clerk/Register how to word the exemption before you submit.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about Cass County, Michigan?
sections.html:
Cass County is part of the South Bend-Mishawaka metropolitan area, a part of southwest Michigan often called Michiana. Cassopolis is the county seat and was platted in 1831 at the geographic center of the county. Dowagiac is the largest city. The villages are Cassopolis, Edwardsburg, Marcellus and Vandalia. The county was formed in 1829 and settled fast because its prairie land was less wooded than nearby areas. Quakers who settled Penn Township in 1829 made it a station on the Underground Railroad, and Southwestern Michigan College sits in Dowagiac.

Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population at 51,677 on 490 square miles of land, or 105.3 people per square mile. The county has 26,087 housing units and 21,207 households. Owner occupancy is 81.6%, the median owner-occupied value is $218,000, median gross rent is $916 and median household income is $70,443. Some 24.0% of residents are 65 or older, and the average commute is 24.4 minutes.

The $218,000 median here sits well above the $162,800 reported for Calhoun County, so a typical Cass County sale carries a larger transfer tax bill in dollars. Check the table above before you set a price.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Cass County?
faqs.a: It costs $30 per document, with $3 more for each extra instrument on a document that assigns or discharges several. The $5 treasurer tax certification for a warranty deed can be included in the same check.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Cass County, Michigan?
faqs.a: Take it to the Clerk/Register office at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, in Cassopolis, or call 269-445-4464. Do not staple your check to the document.

faqs.q: Can I search Cass County deeds for free?
faqs.a: Yes for the index. You can search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number at no charge, but viewing, printing or saving a document costs $1 per page plus a processing fee.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a $218,000 house in Cass County?
faqs.a: It is $1,874.80: $239.80 for the county and $1,635.00 for the state. The county charges 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 of value or fraction.

faqs.q: Does Cass County require a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Generally no. The county asks for a treasurer certification on warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a covenant of warranty, and MCL 211.135 excludes conveyances with no warranty covenant.
